From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Discovery Recap & PoC Onboarding - Finova

Hi Alex / Priya -

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our call and proposed PoC/onboarding plan so we're all aligned.

Key pain points you shared:
- High inference cost and inconsistent latency on peak hours for your doc-classification pipeline.
- Existing infra is a mix of Java backend services (on-prem) and Node.js front-end APIs in GCP.
- Need for model version control and predictable fallbacks during peak trading windows.

Goals / success criteria for the PoC:
- Integration: basic inference end-to-end for the classification workflow (ingest -> inference -> label store).
- Performance: 95th pct latency < 120ms for 512-token classification prompts in our test harness.
- Cost/ops: guidance that reduces per-token cost by at least 30% vs current setup or clear routing plan to lower unit economics.
- Security: SOC2 evidence and ability to run in a VPC if required for production.

Current stack (from call):
- Java microservices (primary inference clients)
- Node.js front-end for sampling and QA tools
- GCP-hosted data store, with some on-prem ETL windows

Proposed PoC & milestones (3-4 week timeline):
- Week 0 (kickoff): alignment on access, sample dataset, and PoC success criteria (owners: Marissa / Alex)
- Week 1 (integration): Ben to provide SDK quickstart + Postman collection; Finova engineers to wire server-side calls (Java via REST) and client-side Node samples (owner: Ben / Finova eng lead)
- Week 2 (tuning & load): Run sample workload, tune batching/cache and measure latency/cost; Redwood to recommend quantization/configs
- Week 3 (eval & decision): Run acceptance tests, review metrics, decide next steps (Dedicated vs Hosted)

Owners / contacts:
- Marissa Cole (AE, marissa@redwood.ai) - commercial lead, kickoff/project manager
- Ben Carter (SE, ben@redwood.ai) - technical onboarding, SDKs, Postman collection
- Alex Johnson (Finova) - eng lead / primary technical owner
- Priya Singh (Finova) - product owner / success criteria sign-off

Next meeting: propose kickoff Wed 2026-06-24 10:00 AM PT (call + share initial sample dataset). Please confirm availability or suggest an alternate slot.

Attachments: finova_poc_plan.pdf (PoC plan), api_compatibility_matrix.xlsx (current API/SDK mapping)

Thanks - looking forward to getting started.

--

Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. A couple items to clarify from our side: 

1) Java support: Our core inference callers are Java services. Do you provide a first-class Java SDK or should we expect to use the REST endpoints from Java?
2) Data residency & SLA: For production we'll likely need US-only data residency and an SLA that covers latency/uptime. Is that covered under Hosted, or do we need Dedicated/Private?
3) Security questionnaire: We'll send a short security questionnaire tomorrow; happy to review SOC2 paperwork.

We're generally aligned on the goals. The proposed timeline looks good - we should confirm availability for the kickoff.

Thanks -

Subject: Re: Discovery Recap & PoC Onboarding - Finova

Alex - great questions. Short answers below and next steps. Full tech details to follow from Ben.

1) Java support: We don't currently ship a first-party Java native SDK library, but our REST API is fully supported from Java (we've got examples and a community-contributed Java client we can share). For the PoC we recommend using the REST integration from your Java services; Ben will include a Java example in the Postman/quickstart bundle.

2) Data residency & SLA: Hosted (our public API) supports region routing and we can route traffic to US regions for data residency during PoC. For SLA-backed guarantees and strict data isolation we typically recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private for production (we can discuss tradeoffs during the PoC).

3) Security docs: we'll share SOC2 and an evidence pack. If you prefer, we can start with hosted-region routing and then evaluate Dedicated for production.

Acceptance criteria (concrete):
- Latency: 95th < 120ms on the sample workload
- Correctness: same label precision/recall within 2% of your baseline on the sample dataset
- Operational: templated rollout plan and fallback to a smaller model under load

Ben will send:
- Postman collection + Java/Node examples
- Quickstart SDK snippets (Python/Node) and guidance for Java REST calls
- A short load test script and measurement instructions

Next steps:
- Ben to share the quickstart and collection by EOD Monday 2026-06-16 (attachment: se_postman_collection.json)
- Alex / Finova to confirm sample dataset + kickoff availability by EOD Friday 2026-06-19
- Kickoff: Wed 2026-06-24 10:00 AM PT (pending confirmation)

Attachments included for reference: api_compatibility_matrix.xlsx (mapping of your clients to Redwood endpoints)

If that all looks right I'll lock in the kickoff time.
